result.stdout:
cxagent — a terminal AI coding agent

USAGE
  cxagent [options]

  Run it in the folder you want to work in, then type what you want in plain    
  language. Reading and writing inside that folder is free; anything outside it,
  and every shell command, asks first.                                          

OPTIONS
  --model NAME            Start on a named provider instance from config.json   
                          instead of the default. The status line shows which   
                          one is live.                                          
  --theme NAME            Start in a named theme, case-insensitive. An unknown  
                          name falls back to 'cxagent' rather than refusing to  
                          start. Available themes: Amber, Crimson, cxagent,     
                          Daylight, Forest, ModernGray, Ocean, Slate            
  --mode MODE             How the agent works: single, fan-out. Fan-out lets it 
                          hand work to sub-agents; single keeps everything in   
                          one agent. Default: fan-out.                          
  --config-dir DIR        Use DIR for config.json, history and session state    
                          instead of the usual location. Useful for a throwaway 
                          setup that leaves your real one alone.                
  -c, --continue          Reopen the most recent session in this folder.        
  -r, --resume ID         Reopen that session. Without an id, the TUI starts    
                          with this folder's sessions listed, to pick from.     
  --sessions [all]        List this folder's sessions and exit. 'all' lists     
                          every folder's.                                       
  --mock                  Run against a scripted provider instead of a real     
                          model. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is spent. 
  -v, --version           Print the version and exit.                           
  -h, --help              Prin
[truncated]
